name: Alila Bangsar Kuala Lumpur
positioning: Contemporary high-rise hotel perched above Kuala Lumpur's Bangsar district, with rooms on the 35th to 40th floors and sweeping city views
best_for: Travelers who want skyline views and a calm base close to the LRT
Guests interested in hands-on Malaysian cultural workshops

facts.text: The hotel is perched high above the Bangsar district with sweeping views of the city.
The hotel is moments from Kuala Lumpur's culinary hotspots, cultural enclaves and main transit lines.
Bangsar LRT station is 0.22 kilometers from the hotel, and KL Sentral is 1.4 kilometers away.
Many rooms have separate sitting areas, rainfall showers and spacious balconies.
The Alila Suite is a one-bedroom suite with a king bed, a separate living and dining area, and a balcony.
The Junior Suite is a corner room with a king bed and a separate sitting area.
The hotel has an outdoor pool and a fitness center with cardio and strength-training equipment.
Alila Moments include a sound bath with traditional handpan and singing bowls.
A terrarium workshop lets guests build their own terrarium and take it home.
Le Comptoir is a high-rise bar and lounge with city views, artisanal cocktails and petite plates.
Botanica + Co is an all-day ground-floor restaurant where lush plants give the feeling of a greenhouse.

highlights.text: All rooms and suites occupy the 35th to 40th floors, with uninterrupted views of the Kuala Lumpur skyline.
The Bangsar Suite is a corner suite with a king bed and a separate living area with city skyline views.
Alila Moments include a Malaysian origami session exploring traditional folds and cultural symbolism.
A Peranakan beading workshop teaches the symbolism, history and craft of the beadwork, and guests stitch their own piece.
Entier serves French plates in a communal dining setting on the 41st floor, with a nose-to-tail approach.

considerations.text: Kuala Lumpur International Airport is 54.9 kilometers from the hotel.
The setting is a city high-rise above the Bangsar district rather than a resort.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's upscale positioning.
